newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin orders swift end to army's funding problem.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin orders swift end to army's funding problem.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin ordered the government on Thursday to take concrete measures to resolve funding problems in the army, where many soldiers have not been paid for months.

"I am very worried about the situation in the armed forces," Yeltsin said in a radio address to the nation. "This situation must not be dragged out any longer," he said, adding that a meeting of defence officials to be chaired by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin should come up with "concrete decisions".
The meeting of defence officials, due to take place on Friday, follows dire warnings by security chief Alexander Lebed that the army is on the brink of mutiny.

In a sign of how seriously the leadership views the problem, Yeltsin discussed it with Defence Minister Igor Rodionov on Saturday and again on Thursday morning. Ministers were also due to discuss the issue at a meeting later in the day.

"I am taking this issue under special control," Yeltsin said. "Russia must have a modern and professional army. Serving in it must be a source of respect and prestige, both for the man in the ranks and to the officer. We will achieve this."
